03770ad0b8b8812b80277fd3431e1f54022e2a97uni.universefireuni.universefire@gmail.comuni.universefireuni.universefire@gmail.com17896264352026-09-17T18:27:15+12:00bb48c91df9c6b4d9ca570bab7bea96d0232ac647mcpw-ybs.4: key the launcher lock + mutexes per workspaceThe FIRST-WINS single-instance guard was machine-global: one lock file at
%LOCALAPPDATA%\watchers\###1-launcher.lock and the bare mutex names
Global\VAD_Watchers_Launcher / Global\VAD_Watchers_Takeover. A launcher
started for a SECOND repository therefore contended with the first repo's live
launcher - it either exited 0 and never opened its own pane grid, or took the
lock over through Stop-PriorLauncherInstances and killed the other repo's
watchers.

Now keyed by the canonical 8-char workspace key from
Modules/watcher_workspace.ps1:

  %LOCALAPPDATA%\watchers\<key>\###1-launcher.lock
  Global\VAD_Watchers_Launcher_<key>
  Global\VAD_Watchers_Takeover_<key>

The key is a DIRECTORY component and the lock file name is unchanged, the same
shape Modules\watcher_teardown.ps1 already uses for teardown-state.json, so
the two cannot drift into different key conventions and every literal
'###1-launcher.lock' match keeps working.

Both names are passed in as parameters (-MutexName / -TakeoverMutexName) and
rebuilt from VAD_WATCHERS_WORKSPACE_KEY when absent. Neither falls back to the
bare legacy name: an empty key degrades to '_default', and to the literal
'default' before it can reach Join-Path, because collapsing back to a
machine-global name is the exact hazard being removed.

The PowerShell.Exiting handler now bakes the keyed name into its scriptblock,
so a repo releases its OWN mutex instead of another repo's.

Global\VAD_Grepai_Heal is deliberately left machine-global, with the reason
recorded in the source: it only serialises a heal, the loser skips a tick
rather than killing anything, and keying a genuinely shared index would allow
two concurrent writers.

Adds tests/launcher_lock_keying.tests.ps1 (16 Pester 3.4.0 tests). The keying
lines are extracted from the launcher and executed, so the assertions run the
real code rather than a hand-copy.

Also updates the two callers that still pointed at the un-keyed lock path:
T21 in tests/launcher_tests.ps1 (computes the keyed path and creates the keyed
parent dir before opening its holder FileStream) and the cleanup in
tests/launcher_wrapper_stack.tests.ps1 (which had been silently cleaning a
path that no longer exists since .2a).

Staged with the hunk-filtered git apply --cached discipline: the concurrent
session's graphiti hunks in the same file remain unstaged.

Gate: 58 assertions across 6 suites, 0 failures, counted by [+]/[-] markers
(see HANDOVER section 2a - the exit code and the trailing summary both
report green for a red suite).

e21a4d4b2d1097ac8561bd65b31ddbebb27b198auni.universefireuni.universefire@gmail.comuni.universefireuni.universefire@gmail.com17896227902026-09-17T17:26:30+12:00ef08919ee71af72bca203378a3fad6b4cc3746f5mcpw-ybs.2b: make startup orphan sweep fail-safe per workspaceThe startup orphan sweep at the tail of Stop-PriorLauncherInstances is a
FALLBACK for orphans the PID-scoped Stop-AllWatchers could not reach. It
terminated ANY machine-wide process matching a sweep pattern; the
graphify-rs.exe entry carries an empty Pattern (match-all), so two repos
launched at once could tree-kill each other's live watchers.

Now the sweep consults Test-WatchersProcessAttribution (new, in
Modules/watcher_workspace.ps1) before terminating: a candidate is killed only
when its command line carries this workspace's 8-char key or its absolute root;
otherwise it is skipped and counted in $sweepSkipped. Fail-safe by design:
an orphan is harmless, a sibling repo's live watcher is not.

- Modules/watcher_workspace.ps1: add Test-WatchersProcessAttribution
- ###1...ps1: attribute candidates in the sweep; add $sweepSkipped counter
- tests/launcher_sweep_attribution.tests.ps1: 16 Pester 3.4.0 tests that
  extract the real sweep block and run it against a stubbed process table
